title.justification: The paper focuses on the effects of using smaller batch sizes in deep reinforcement learning, which involves replay memories and gradient updates.
title.quote: In this work we present a broad empirical study that suggests reducing the batch size can result in a number of significant performance gains...

extractions.description: The paper explores the impact of batch size on the performance of deep reinforcement learning algorithms. It presents a comprehensive empirical study showing that smaller batch sizes can lead to improved performance, better exploration, and reduced computational cost. The study examines various reinforcement learning agents, architectures, and training regimens to highlight these effects and suggests potential underlying causes.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The study is primarily focused on the efficiency of algorithms in reinforcement learning, specifically in adjusting batch sizes, which does not relate directly to Climate Change themes.
climate_change_is_central.quote: The impact of our findings and analyses go beyond the choice of the batch size hyper-parameter, and help us develop a better understanding of the learning dynamics in online deep RL.
